Theme

School & learning

demonstrative adjective

in grammar

also demonstrative pronoun, demonstratives, demonstrative adjective

modern

Traupman 224, 246

1dēmōnstrātīvus: long o before nstr (Lewis & Short dēmonstrātīvus, unmarked). Vowels before ns are long (Cic. Or. 159), as in mōnstrum, dēmōnstrō.

dēmōnstrātīvus1, dēmōnstrātīva, dēmōnstrātīvum

declension

prōnōmen dēmōnstrātīvum: hic, ille (Traupman 224). Lewis & Short gives the word only in rhetoric (the oratory of praise and blame) and of the forefinger; we have not found the grammatical sense there. Varro calls hic and quis articulī (see article).

Examples

  • Dā exempla prōnōminis dēmōnstrātīvī. — Hic, ille.

    Give some examples of a demonstrative pronoun. — This one, that one.Traupman 224

See also pronoun, article, this, that.

SourcesLewis & Short: demonstrativus

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 224, 246.
